scope: frida-java 2.0 candidate evaluation, local Linux x86-64 JDK 27 only; no production integration selected

report.result: candidate remains usable for low-level FFM symbol access; high-level lifecycle wrappers do not satisfy deterministic ownership as supplied
report.selection_status: under_evaluation; availability passed, lifecycle behavior and callback teardown unverified
report.source_identity: source-identity.json; all 12 relevant released2.0 files equal pinned commit cdc18821ac15a13c9aea76d3dc9f61cc0fe313bf

usable_sequences.sequence: script.unload(); finally script.clean(); preserve unload error and add any cleanup error as suppressed
usable_sequences.qualification: Improves failure visibility; clean does not remove Closure static registrations, so this is not complete callback lifecycle closure.

usable_sequences.sequence: Use public FridaLibraryLoader.findFunction(name, FunctionDescriptor) against its single loaded library; retain raw native pointers at creation; call explicit close/detach/unref with owned references. FridaNativeUtils.fridaUnref is also public.
usable_sequences.qualification: No reflection, private-field access or clone modification is needed if pointers are owned from creation rather than obtained through high-level factories.

usable_sequences.sequence: Closure.connectClosure(rawObject, signal, callback) returns handlerId. Disconnect the native handler first through g_signal_handler_disconnect, quiesce in-flight callbacks, then Closure.disconnectClosure(handlerId). Retain object pointer and handler ID in the Java owner.
usable_sequences.qualification: Native disconnect lookup is available. A quiescence mechanism and real callback lifecycle proof are still required; the helper itself only removes Java maps.

usable_sequences.sequence: After every native owner, signal and callback is finished, public findFunction can invoke frida_shutdown and frida_deinit. Do not use high-level Frida classes afterward.
usable_sequences.qualification: Both terminal calls returned in the two availability JVMs. No manager/session/script resources were created by this probe.

concrete_conflicts.conflict: close catches every FridaException from unload and logs it as possibly normal. Explicit unload plus clean preserves that failure.

Session close detaches without unref; DeviceManager close invokes native close without unref. Session has no public raw pointer accessor; manager getPointer is package-private. Normal factory-created wrappers therefore cannot be fully released through their exposed external lifecycle methods.

Script clean clears handler IDs and unrefs its native pointer but never removes ACTIVE_CLOSURES or the associated static maps. No native finalize notifier invokes cleanupClosureByPointer. The retained message callback can retain Script through its bound hijackMessage method. on returns no handler ID and no off method is provided.

Upcall stub has JVM lifetime and user callback exceptions inside the switch are caught. Pointer/map/log/array preparation precedes that catch, so the entire upcall is not protected. Registration publishes callback data after native connection, leaving an emission-before-publication race to verify.
handleError retains only error text, frees GError, and throws FridaException. Domain/code are lost. Typed recovery requires reading them at the lower-level GError boundary before free.

Loaded library and marshal stub use Arena.global. The high-level deinit operation is commented out. Raw shutdown/deinit can end a one-shot native lifetime but do not reset Frida.isInitialized, remove static callback registrations or unload the global library.

callback_and_dispatch_contract.ownership: Closure static maps strongly retain callback objects. MARSHAL_STUB remains alive for JVM lifetime.
callback_and_dispatch_contract.delivery: handleScriptMessageMarshal converts native message data to String and byte[] before invoking the callback synchronously on the emitting native thread; there is no Java executor handoff.
callback_and_dispatch_contract.main_context: No main-context/loop implementation is present in binding Java sources. Examples wait on Java sleep/latches. Native Frida initialization supplies its runtime, but callback dispatch context and teardown quiescence are not established by this source review. Lower-level frida_get_main_context and g_main_loop_* symbols are available.
callback_and_dispatch_contract.allocation_thread_boundary: Keep these controller signal callbacks separate from target allocation hooks. No target allocator callback was introduced or executed.

native_version_and_loader.supported_override: Before first loader/class initialization, use its bins directory under the process working directory, with Linux x86-64 name libfrida-core-x86_64.so. This source-supported lookup precedes classifier resources and system fallback.
safety_conditions: Own the working directory/bins entry and verify the producer hash before launch.
Require Frida.getVersion to equal17.24.3; loader itself has no version lock and can fall back after a bins load error.
Use a native producer exporting the required symbols. A version-only shim is not such a producer.
Treat the global library as process-lifetime; no supported Path/Arena injection or deterministic unload method is exposed.
native_version_and_loader.initial_override_failure: Version-only producer loaded, but initialization failed because frida_version_string was not dynamically exported; nm confirmed it was a local symbol. This is a producer conflict, not a rejection of frida-java.
native_version_and_loader.corrected_override: Parent-provided exported-symbol producer java-allocation-control-DhX22B/libattach-probe.so loaded through the same bins entry and passed.

packaging_comparison.suppression: none; SLF4J missing-provider warnings also retained

executed_gates.ABI_scope: Linux x86-64 only; successful handle creation is availability, not functional ABI validation on all platforms

report.dependencies: dependencies/acquisition.json; released frida-java2.0 plus its declared SLF4J2.0.17 API. Jackson-dependent classes were not exercised; full dependency closure remains unverified.
report.decision: Do not reject candidate solely for Script.close or missing high-level deinit: lower-level public APIs can express error-preserving ownership and shutdown. Retain as a candidate for a Java-owned boundary that uses raw owned pointers. Full high-level wrappers require lifecycle repairs or bypasses; callback quiescence, typed errors and supported-platform behavior remain acceptance gates.
report.scope: No clone/project edits, native rebuilds, remote operations, attachment or allocation reruns. Only fresh scratch evidence writes and the authorized release availability probes.
report.retention: Parent /root owns final clone and evaluation-root cleanup after archival.

next_gate: Exercise attachment, authentic script callbacks, allocation waiting and terminal cleanup through the selected public lower-level Java/FFM API without the scratch C controller adapter. Preserve typed native errors and callback lifetime guarantees; successful symbol lookup alone does not select the integration.

cleanup.evaluation_root: Retained for the lower-level integration gate; remove after its accepted evidence handoff.
cleanup.clone: Parent-owned pinned clone and acquired release artifacts retained for next consumer; remove after selection evidence is durable.
